the pattern nobody names

There's no fight.
No goodbye.

Just the slow discovery that the last real conversation already happened — months ago, and neither of you noticed the room go quiet.

the part nobody says out loud

Somewhere around 32, I stopped choosing people. I started waiting to be chosen — keeping a silent ledger where reaching out felt like spending, and I'd decided the balance was his job to fix.

the belief I had to bury

I used to think real friendship survives on its own — six months dark, pick up right where you left off. Then my dad landed in the hospital and I didn't know whose life to call.

Depth is what you had. Frequency is what keeps it from becoming past tense.

the exact move that works

"Hey, we should catch up sometime" hands the other person a chore. It asks them to remember why you mattered.

I texted a screenshot of a bug we'd spent a weekend fixing: "still think about how we almost quit over this." He replied in four minutes.

sit with this

The fade is almost never someone walking away from you.

It's two people standing still, each too proud to be the one who admits they noticed.
